description: Value/theme codebook shared by Part 1 (stated values on About pages) and Part 2 (disclosures), so that Part 3 can compare the two on identical categories. Hybrid design: six culture values adapted from the MIT Sloan 'Big Nine' corporate values, four stakeholder/ESG themes from stakeholder theory, plus Safety.

sources.big_nine: Sull, D., Turconi, S., & Sull, C. (2020). When it comes to culture, does your company walk the talk? MIT Sloan Management Review (Culture 500). The 'Big Nine' values most often stated by large U.S. companies: agility, collaboration, customer, diversity, execution, innovation, integrity, performance, respect.
sources.stated_values_precedent: Guiso, L., Sapienza, P., & Zingales, L. (2015). The value of corporate culture. Journal of Financial Economics, 117(1), 60-76. Coded values stated on S&P 500 company websites; motivates studying stated vs. lived values.
sources.stakeholder: Freeman, R. E. (1984). Strategic Management: A Stakeholder Approach; Business Roundtable (2019), Statement on the Purpose of a Corporation (customers, employees, suppliers, communities, shareholders).

categories.name: Innovation
categories.definition: Commitment to creating new products, technologies, ideas or ways of working; pioneering, invention, research and development, adaptability and speed of change.
categories.include: 'we push the boundaries of what is possible', R&D, breakthrough science, reinventing, agility
categories.exclude: A bare product list or product description with no claim about innovating as a value or identity

categories.name: Integrity & ethics
categories.definition: Honesty, ethical conduct, transparency, accountability, compliance, doing the right thing, trust and trustworthiness.
categories.include: 'we act with integrity', code of conduct, 'doing the right thing', transparency, accountability
categories.exclude: Data privacy or security mentioned only as a product feature

categories.name: Customer focus
categories.definition: Putting customers, clients or patients first; service, customer satisfaction, listening to and meeting customer needs.
categories.include: 'customer obsession', 'clients come first', 'patients at the center', service excellence
categories.exclude: Merely naming who the customers are (e.g. 'we serve 50 million customers') without a commitment to them

categories.name: Collaboration & teamwork
categories.definition: Working together across teams, partnership, one-team culture, cooperation with colleagues and partners.
categories.include: 'one team', 'we win together', partnership with customers/partners as a way of working
categories.exclude: Business partnerships or alliances described only as commercial deals

categories.name: Performance & results
categories.definition: Delivering results, excellence, operational execution, quality, growth, financial performance and shareholder value, leadership position.
categories.include: 'deliver superior returns', 'operational excellence', 'industry leader', quality, efficiency, disciplined capital allocation
categories.exclude: Plain factual statistics (revenue, headcount) with no framing of performance as a value or goal

categories.name: Respect & people
categories.definition: Treating people with respect, dignity, care and fairness; valuing people as a cultural norm.
categories.include: 'we treat everyone with respect', 'people are our greatest asset', caring culture
categories.exclude: Specific workforce programmes (code those as employee_wellbeing_development) and diversity statements (code as diversity_inclusion)

categories.name: Diversity, equity & inclusion
categories.origin: Big Nine: diversity; ESG social pillar
categories.definition: Diversity of people and perspectives, inclusion, equity, belonging, equal opportunity, representation of under-represented groups.
categories.include: DEI, inclusion, belonging, diverse workforce/suppliers, racial equity, gender equality, accessibility for people with disabilities
categories.exclude: Diversity of products or business lines

categories.name: Environment & sustainability
categories.definition: Protecting the environment and planet; climate, emissions, net zero, energy transition, renewable energy, resource use, waste, water, biodiversity.
categories.include: 'carbon negative by 2030', net zero, lower-carbon energy, sustainable sourcing, environmental stewardship
categories.exclude: 'Sustainable growth' or 'sustainable returns' used only in a financial sense

categories.name: Community & social impact
categories.origin: Stakeholder theory (communities, society) / ESG social pillar
categories.definition: Positive impact on communities and society beyond the business; philanthropy, volunteering, access, economic opportunity, corporate citizenship, purpose for society.
categories.include: giving programmes, foundations, 'improving lives', access to medicines, community investment, education initiatives

categories.name: Employee wellbeing & development
categories.definition: Commitments to the workforce: training, careers and development, pay and benefits, health and wellbeing, engagement, great place to work.
categories.include: 'invest in our people', career growth, benefits, wellbeing programmes, employee engagement
categories.exclude: General respect/dignity language (respect_people); recruiting calls-to-action ('Join us') alone

categories.name: Safety
categories.origin: Added for sector salience (Energy, Healthcare, Industrials)
categories.definition: Physical safety of workers, customers, patients and communities; process safety, product and patient safety, health and safety culture.
categories.include: 'safety is our top priority', zero incidents, patient safety, product safety, operational/process safety
categories.exclude: Cybersecurity or financial 'safety' (integrity_ethics or not coded)

coding_rules.present: A category is present only if the page expresses it as something the company values, commits to, or identifies with - not if a word merely appears.
coding_rules.salience: 1 = mentioned (present but not central); 2 = emphasized (headline, repeated, or framed as a core value/mission).
coding_rules.evidence: Every present category must be supported by a verbatim quote from the page.
